clue.text: Cramped accommodation for a clerical dignitary, perhaps ?

definitions.text: Cramped accommodation for a clerical dignitary, perhaps

parts.words: Cramped accommodation for a clerical dignitary, perhaps
parts.note: a phrase for tight, confined living space, reread as the lodgings of a canon living in a cathedral's enclosed precinct

explanation.surface: A senior churchman is squeezed into a poky little flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathedral 'close' is the walled ground round it where canons and deans live, so their lodgings are quarters in the close; the everyday phrase means a cramped space.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a tight, crowded space is also, read literally, the housing found in a cathedral precinct.

clue.text: They take some unusual positions in the course of their careers

definitions.text: They take some unusual positions in the course of their careers

parts.words: They take some unusual positions in the course of their careers
parts.note: sounds like people with odd jobs or opinions; really performers who bend their bodies into strange shapes

explanation.surface: People who hold surprising posts throughout their working lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Positions' looks like jobs or stances, but it means body postures; these circus performers twist themselves into knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats who bend their limbs into extraordinary postures are known for such feats of flexibility.

clue.text: Root of perfume

definitions.text: Root of perfume

parts.note: not an origin but a real root: the dried rhizome of an iris used in scents

explanation.walkthrough: 'Root' looks figurative (the source of perfume); it is the dried iris rootstock used as a fixative in perfumes.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet-scented rhizome of certain irises is ground for use in perfumery.

clue.text: A good blow-out, maybe

definitions.text: A good blow-out, maybe

parts.note: a blow-out usually means a big feast, but here it is literally blowing air out of the lungs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow-out' suggests a slap-up meal; taken literally it is a long breath out.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out is the act of expelling air from the lungs.

clue.text: Antony was, by Eros

definitions.text: Antony was, by Eros

parts.note: in Antony and Cleopatra, Antony orders his servant Eros to take off his armour

explanation.surface: Suggests Mark Antony was conquered by the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Eros seems to be the god of love; in Antony and Cleopatra he is Antony's servant, told 'Unarm, Eros', who strips off his armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped of armour or weapons, Antony was left defenceless.

clue.text: Deciphered speeches booked in war-time

definitions.text: booked in war-time

indicators.note: read as de-ciphered: the cipher, meaning a nought, is taken out of the word for speeches

parts.note: orations are formal speeches

explanation.surface: Wartime messages decoded and logged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deciphered' looks like decoded; it means with the cipher (an old word for zero, the letter O) removed from ORATIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime food allowances were recorded in ration books, so these quotas were literally booked.

clue.text: If he put on a stone, he might still, be light!

definitions.text: If he put on a stone, he might still, be light!

parts.words: If he put on a stone, he might still, be light!
parts.note: adding stone to a whirlpool's name gives a famous lighthouse rock off Plymouth

explanation.surface: Even after gaining fourteen pounds, a man might still be slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on a stone' looks like weight gain; add STONE to the name and you get the Eddystone, the lighthouse off Plymouth, so 'he' would be a light.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool or swirl of water also serves as a man's name, and with stone added it names a lighthouse.

clue.text: Not what is generally meant by a lean period

definitions.text: Not what is generally meant by a lean period

parts.words: Not what is generally meant by a lean period
parts.note: lean usually means meagre, but here thin as an extra, unused span of hours

explanation.surface: A lean period isn't what people usually think.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lean period' normally means hard times; 'spare' also means lean or thin, so the hours you have free fit the words in another sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Free hours away from work are leisure, and spare also means thin.

clue.text: The man to go to for a dip

definitions.text: The man to go to for a dip

parts.words: The man to go to for a dip
parts.note: a dip is a cheap candle made by dipping a wick in fat, sold by a tradesman in such candles

explanation.surface: Someone you'd visit to arrange a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dip' suggests a swim; it was also a cheap candle made by dipping a wick in animal fat, sold by this tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker and seller of fat candles, called dips, was the old tradesman in that line.

clue.text: No threats can come from this quarter

definitions.text: quarter

indicators.note: the answer's letters can be produced from the words that precede, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A reassurance that no danger will arrive from a particular direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can come from' tells you to rearrange NO THREATS; 'quarter' is a compass point, not a district.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter of the compass is one of its directions, and this is the one between two cardinal points.

clue.text: Meredith's eponymous character who might have enjoyed these puzzles?

definitions.text: Meredith's eponymous character who might have enjoyed these puzzles?

parts.words: Meredith's eponymous character who might have enjoyed these puzzles?
parts.note: George Meredith wrote a novel named after its heroine 'of the Crossways', and crossways suggests crosswords

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel's heroine imagined as a fan of this very crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: George Meredith's novel 'Diana of the Crossways' (1885) is named for its heroine; 'crossways' is played as if it meant crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the Meredith novel is identified by her name alone.

clue.text: Mostly a river bird

definitions.text: Mostly a river bird

parts.note: a bird whose name, less its final letter, spells a Yorkshire river, so the bird is mostly a river

explanation.surface: A bird that spends most of its time by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bird found mostly by rivers; in fact the bird's name loses its last letter to give the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This blackbird or thrush relative is a member of the thrush family whose name minus L gives the Ouse.

clue.text: The governess of floods, according to Titania

definitions.text: The governess of floods, according to Titania

parts.words: The governess of floods, according to Titania
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the fairy queen calls the night's ruling body that controls the tides 'the governess of floods'

explanation.surface: A fairy queen names a female ruler of the waters.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, Titania says 'the moon, the governess of floods, pale in her anger, washes all the air'.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavenly body that governs the tides is described by Titania as ruler of the floods.

clue.text: Where Manxmen strip ?

definitions.text: Where Manxmen
definitions.meaning: a town on the west coast of the Isle of Man, home to Manx people

definitions.text: strip
definitions.meaning: to strip is to take off the skin or outer layer

explanation.definitionFit: Peel is a port town on the Isle of Man, and to remove an outer skin is to strip it.

clue.text: Where to find a smart canoe in California

definitions.text: Where to find a smart canoe in California

indicators.note: the letters of the following words can be found rearranged in the answer

explanation.surface: A stylish boat is to be found in a Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where to find' signals that SMART CANOE, rearranged, is the place; the city sits on the Sacramento River, so a canoe there is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of California lies on a river where canoes are common, and its letters hold the rearranged phrase.

clue.text: Behaved like 1 dn, on the dance floor ?

definitions.text: Behaved like 1 dn, on the dance floor ?

parts.words: Behaved like 1 dn, on the dance floor ?
parts.note: performers who bend their bodies into knots coil and wrench themselves, and a 1960s dance shares that name

explanation.surface: Someone dances as though made of rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Down's performers bend their bodies about; on the dance floor the same past tense names doing the 1960s dance craze, the Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: To contort the body is to wrench it round, and the same verb names a popular 1960s dance.

clue.text: Getting a tanning I'd be upset and angry

definitions.text: angry

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the words before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Being thrashed would leave me cross and resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like part of the definition; it is the signal to rearrange TANNING I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious at an injustice is resentful and cross.

clue.text: Main prospect on the Isle of Wight

definitions.text: Main prospect on the Isle of Wight

parts.words: Main prospect on the Isle of Wight
parts.note: main means the ocean and prospect means a vista; together they name a village on the island

explanation.surface: Describes the chief outlook from England's south-coast island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, as in 'the Spanish Main', and 'prospect' a view; Seaview is also a village on the Isle of Wight, the island off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista over the ocean is also the name of a seaside village on the island.

clue.text: The things they give them to do in Strangeways Gaol ?

definitions.text: The things they give them to do in Strangeways Gaol ?

parts.words: The things they give them to do in Strangeways Gaol ?
parts.note: Strangeways is a Manchester prison, and its name read as strange ways suggests peculiar little tasks

explanation.surface: Asks what work prisoners are set in a Manchester jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Strangeways is a prison in Manchester; its name split as 'strange ways' points to tasks that are peculiar, i.e. odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Small miscellaneous tasks are casual pieces of work, and 'strange' is another word for odd.

clue.text: Simple inset illustrating drink

annotationWithheld.why: Simple inset illustrating drink: the parse needs 'inset' split as 'in set', HERB (simple) in SET, so the one printed word gives both the container signal and SET; the scan prints 'inset'.

clue.text: Swift cry

definitions.text: Swift cry

parts.note: not a quick shout but the call of the swift, a bird known for its shrill screaming

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like an adjective meaning fast; it is the bird, whose call is a piercing scream.
explanation.definitionFit: The swift's call is a harsh, high-pitched shriek.

clue.text: High' colour

definitions.text: High' colour

parts.note: not a flushed face but the hue of the heavens overhead

explanation.definitionFit: The light blue of a clear sky is the colour found up high.

clue.text: He had use for a handkerchief

definitions.text: He had use for a handkerchief

parts.words: He had use for a handkerchief
parts.note: in Othello the villain plants Desdemona's handkerchief to fake her infidelity

explanation.surface: A man who found a hanky handy.
explanation.walkthrough: Not someone with a cold: in Shakespeare's Othello the villain uses Desdemona's handkerchief as false proof of her affair with Cassio.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's scheming ensign exploits the lost handkerchief to destroy the Moor.

clue.text: You can depend on a broken instrument

definitions.text: depend

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the stringed instrument are rearranged

parts.note: a lyre is a small harp-like stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Wry advice that a damaged instrument will never let you down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' tells you to rearrange LYRE, the instrument the clue does not name; 'on' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone is to trust or count on them.

clue.text: Two generations in the building trade

definitions.text: in the building trade

parts.note: a mother is the elder of two generations
a son is the younger generation

explanation.surface: A family firm of builders runs from parent to child.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives both pieces: MA, a mother, and SON, her child, make two generations.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker or bricklayer is a craftsman in construction.

clue.text: She made a brave choice when she married

definitions.text: She made a brave choice when she married

parts.words: She made a brave choice when she married
parts.note: brave as a noun, an old term for a Native American warrior, whose wife was given a now-offensive name

explanation.surface: A woman showed courage in her choice of husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' seems to mean courageous; it is the old term for a Native American warrior, and the answer is the dated, now offensive word for his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The dated term, now considered offensive, for a Native American woman or wife.

clue.text: The beginning of the end, in a purely personal sense'

definitions.text: in a purely personal sense

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the word end is wanted

explanation.surface: A grand phrase about the start of the finish, made personal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The beginning of the end' looks like a set phrase; it is THE plus the first letter of 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The old second-person pronoun is the intimate, personal form of address.

clue.text: 21's purse, in his own estimation

definitions.text: 21's purse, in his own estimation

parts.note: in Othello the villain says that whoever steals his purse steals rubbish

explanation.surface: A villain rates his own wallet as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the villain of Othello, who says 'Who steals my purse steals trash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago's line calls his purse worthless rubbish.

clue.text: Served with a double helping of tongue ?

definitions.text: Served with a double helping of tongue ?

parts.words: Served with a double helping of tongue ?
parts.note: tongue as a meat dish, reread as language: someone given two languages

explanation.surface: A diner is dished up twice the usual portion of tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongue looks like the cold meat; it means a language, and 'bi-' (two) plus 'lingual' (of the tongue) is a speaker of two.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fluent in two languages has, in Latin terms, two tongues.

clue.text: Where one naturally expects acts of violence

definitions.text: Where one naturally expects acts of violence

parts.words: Where one naturally expects acts of violence
parts.note: acts belong in playhouses and violence in combat, so the phrase points to regions of fighting

explanation.surface: Places where brutality is only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts' suggests stage acts, found in theatres; theatres of war are the zones where fighting takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: Military theatres are the areas where combat operations happen.
